answers.question: Q1
answers.answer: XYZ predicts deterministic admission eligibility and possible Jog/Marathon grouping from issue, plan, review, PRS, dependency, freshness, and coordination evidence. Needle predicts the next observed canonical action at the end-of-turn boundary from the current request and prior action history; both can reuse bounded request/history context and canonical labels, but admission facts must remain separate from prediction features and targets. A workflow example can show predictive accuracy, not recommendation usefulness, which requires a later user-facing study.

answers.question: Q2
answers.answer: Needle main reconstructs and logs serialized context but does not call a model; 710c adds detached inference, feedback scoring, and last-result publication. os.replace gives atomic visibility, not freshness: an older worker can still replace a newer same-session result, so test delayed workers with prompt IDs/sequence numbers and verify stale output is rejected and feedback remains attributable.

answers.question: Q3
answers.answer: Neither 44 labels nor 100% parsed outputs certify quality. Needle #12 withdraws the PTQ conclusion and clarifies that 100% was only name extraction; the serializer contract says labels take no arguments, while no_action is represented as an empty answer list, so abstention and an observed semantic no_action must remain distinct during scoring. A current inconsistency is that the serializer maps no_action to answers: [] while the evaluation plan requires explicit separation of empty abstention from semantic no_action.

answers.question: Q4
answers.answer: Deterministic code must perform eligibility, hashes, freshness, dependency/shared-contract and effective-write-set checks, queue leasing, parked-work protection, contract validation, output validation, and authorized writes. Luna may explain evidence, classify candidates, suggest groups, or flag escalation; it must not invent plans, self-approve trusted review, alter PRS, dispatch, or merge. Jog owns queue state, while Marathon owns execution/review/gate/PR state; cmd_jog_add confirms duplicate refusal but can reset terminal rows, so rescans must not call it for parked work.

answers.question: Q5
answers.answer: Use one small frozen, independently adjudicated replay manifest spanning both domains: positive and adversarial admission snapshots plus valid next-action rows, with immutable row/session-family IDs, no future fields, independent labels, nonempty split assertions, and no family/event overlap. Compare Luna against local deterministic baselines and a stronger-model or manual arm on identical rows, checking false acceptance, leakage, coverage, malformed outputs, abstentions, stale responses, and cost/latency; XYZ must separately test writer races, pagination, dependencies, parked work, and grouping safety, while Needle must separately test boundary reconstruction, label support, no_action semantics, and prediction accuracy.

answers.question: Q6
answers.answer: Narrow Luna to extraction or grouping when it misses eligibility/accuracy bars but deterministic gates remain trustworthy; use a stronger model when frozen cases show repeated substantive false accepts or unresolved ambiguity after bounded review; stop when provenance, containment, writer atomicity, or trustworthy labels cannot be established. This tools-prohibited trial is synthetic advisory evidence only and cannot establish production accuracy, latency, dollar cost, privacy/retention behavior, or race guarantees; those require execution-time measurements and fault-injection tests.

limitations: No tools, runtime tests, race injection, API calls, private-corpus evaluation, or production measurements were performed.
